title: Luciferase Reporter Assay
duration: About 3 days (1 day plating, 1–2 days expression, 2 h assay)
purpose: To measure the activity of a promoter, enhancer or signaling pathway in cultured mammalian cells (for example HEK293T) by quantifying firefly luciferase from a test reporter and normalizing it to a co-transfected Renilla luciferase control (dual-luciferase format).
principle: A test construct places firefly luciferase under control of the regulatory element of interest, while a second plasmid drives constitutive Renilla luciferase. Cell lysate is first mixed with a reagent that gives firefly luminescence; a second reagent then quenches the firefly signal and supplies the substrate for Renilla, so both activities are read from the same sample [1]. Dividing firefly by Renilla signal per well corrects for differences in cell number and transfection efficiency [1][2][3]. The signal is read in a luminometer; the assay is sensitive and spans several orders of magnitude [1].

materials.detail: HEK293T (or your cell line) in DMEM with 10% serum; cells should be at most 95% confluent at lysis [1]
Test promoter or response element upstream of firefly luciferase (for example pGL3-based) [3]
For example pRL-TK; keep the reporter:Renilla ratio between 10:1 and 50:1 by mass to avoid trans effects [1][3]
Lipid-based reagent suited to your cells; follow the manufacturer's DNA:reagent ratios
Empty reporter vector (no promoter or response element) and, if available, a positive-control construct or stimulus
Dilute 5× PLB 1:5 with distilled water (1 volume + 4 volumes); fresh is best, 1× is stable about 1 month at 4 °C [1]
Lyophilized substrate reconstituted in the supplied buffer; aliquot and store at −20 °C (1 month) or −70 °C (1 year); warm to room temperature before use [1]
Substrate 1:50 in Stop & Glo Buffer (200 µL per 10 mL) for the Dual-Luciferase kit; make fresh at room temperature [1]

materials.item: White opaque assay plates or tubes
materials.detail: Opaque plates reduce cross-talk between wells [1]

equipment: Luminometer (single-tube or plate reader; avoid scintillation counters)

steps.text: Plate cells so they are 60–70% confluent at transfection [3]. As a starting point, about 1 × 10⁵ HEK293T cells per well of a 24-well plate; adjust for your line.

Set up each transfection in triplicate wells: reporter plasmid plus Renilla plasmid at a 10:1 to 50:1 mass ratio (Bio-protocol used 2 µg:200 ng in a 6-well plate, 10:1) [1][3]. Scale by surface area for 24-well plates.
Add any effector or expression plasmid and the transfection reagent as the manufacturer directs, and add complexes to the cells [3].
Incubate cells at 37 °C, 5% CO₂ for the expression period (48 h in the Bio-protocol example); apply any drug or stimulus for the last hours as required [3].
Remove the medium and gently wash the cells once with PBS; remove all of the rinse [1][3].
Add 1× PLB to cover the cells (24-well: 100 µL; 6-well: 500 µL; 96-well: 20 µL) and rock at room temperature for 15 min [1][3].
Equilibrate LAR II and Stop & Glo to room temperature. Dispense 100 µL LAR II per tube or well of the white plate [1][3].
Transfer up to 20 µL lysate to the LAR II and mix by pipetting 2–3 times; do not vortex the lysate [1].
Read firefly luminescence with a 2 s pre-read delay and a 10 s measurement [1][3].
Add 100 µL Stop & Glo, mix, and read Renilla luminescence the same way (2 s delay, 10 s measurement) [1][3].
Include blank wells (untransfected-cell lysate) to measure background for both readings [1].
Calculate firefly ÷ Renilla for each well, average technical replicates, then divide by the ratio of the control condition (for example the empty vector) to give fold change [1][2][3].

pause: Lysates can be kept for 6 h at room temperature (22 °C), up to 16 h on ice, 1 month at −20 °C and longer at −70 °C; avoid more than 2–3 freeze-thaws [1].
Reconstituted LAR II can be frozen in aliquots and Stop & Glo is best made fresh [1].
results: Firefly and Renilla signals well above the blank (background); the empty-vector ratio gives the basal level.
A promoter or response element that is active increases the firefly/Renilla ratio relative to the empty vector, and a pathway activator or inhibitor shifts it further.
The assay is linear over many orders of magnitude [1]; if readings exceed the luminometer range, dilute the lysate.
controls: Empty reporter vector (no regulatory element) to define basal activity
Untransfected-cell lysate to measure firefly and Renilla background [1]
A positive control (a strongly active promoter or a known pathway stimulus) to confirm the assay works
Renilla co-transfected in every well to normalize for cell number and transfection efficiency [1][2][3]
Identical volumes and medium in background wells and samples [2]

troubleshooting.cause: Poor transfection, low DNA quality, over-confluent cells or too little lysate
troubleshooting.fix: Check transfection, use endotoxin-free DNA, keep confluence under 95%, optimize DNA amount [1]
Use master mixes, normalize to Renilla, increase replicates [1][3]

troubleshooting.problem: Firefly signal falls as Renilla rises
troubleshooting.cause: Strong trans effect from a too-active Renilla plasmid
troubleshooting.fix: Raise the reporter:Renilla ratio toward 50:1 or switch to a weaker control promoter [1][2]

troubleshooting.cause: Residual firefly signal after Stop & Glo
troubleshooting.fix: Matters only if Renilla is more than about 1,000-fold lower; ensure Stop & Glo is fresh [1]

troubleshooting.problem: Signal drifts during a plate read
troubleshooting.fix: Read samples at consistent times, or use the Dual-Glo format, which is stable for about 2 h [2]

safety: The lyophilized luciferase substrate contains dithiothreitol (DTT) and the Stop & Glo substrate contains a volatile solvent: wear gloves, a lab coat and eye protection, and keep caps closed [2].
Handle HEK293T and other human cells at biosafety level 2 in a cabinet; bleach or autoclave all liquid and solid waste that touched cells.
Dispose of used luciferase reagents as chemical waste according to your institution's policy.

references.citation: Promega Corporation. Dual-Luciferase Reporter Assay System, instructions for use of products E1910 and E1960. Technical Manual TM040, revised 8/23.
Promega Corporation. Dual-Glo Luciferase Assay System, instructions for use of products E2920, E2940 and E2980. Technical Manual TM058, revised 1/23.
Tanas MR, Garcia K. Luciferase reporter assay. Bio-protocol Preprint. 2022 May 25.

summary: Dual-luciferase reporter assay in transfected mammalian cells: co-transfect a firefly reporter and a Renilla control, lyse with passive lysis buffer, read both luciferases sequentially in a luminometer and normalize to calculate fold change.
keywords: luciferase reporter assay dual-luciferase firefly Renilla HEK293T transfection promoter activity passive lysis buffer luminometer normalization
